title: Critical Outdoor System Fault
shortDescription: A critical fault in the outdoor unit has shut down the system.
fullDescription:
E200 on Lennox communicating heat pumps (iHarmony / iComfort) indicates a critical outdoor fault that required immediate shutdown. The specific sub-cause is logged in fault history and will typically appear alongside a sub-code (E202, E223, etc.).

Check the iComfort service menu for the secondary code.

fixSteps.title: Read fault history
fixSteps.instruction: Access Service > Alerts on the iComfort UI.

fixSteps.title: Follow sub-code
fixSteps.instruction: Troubleshoot using the secondary code's article.

faq.a: Yes via breaker, but the sub-cause must be fixed.

title: Outdoor Unit Hardware Error
shortDescription: Outdoor control board detected internal hardware failure.
fullDescription: E202 indicates the outdoor board self-test failed. This is typically a failed control board that requires replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace board if persistent
fixSteps.instruction: A tech will install a matching iHarmony control.

faq.a: No - matched to the outdoor model.

title: Outdoor Low Line Voltage
shortDescription: Outdoor unit detected line voltage below 187V.
fullDescription:
E223 is triggered when the outdoor control measures line voltage below safe minimum (~187V on 230V). Operation is blocked until voltage normalizes.

Causes include utility brownouts, loose connections at the disconnect, or a contactor issue.

fixSteps.title: Tighten lugs
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, tighten service lugs.

whenToCallPro: If voltage is fine but fault persists.

faq.a: Yes when voltage returns to normal.

title: Outdoor High Line Voltage
shortDescription: Outdoor unit detected line voltage above 253V.
fullDescription:
E224 is triggered when incoming line voltage exceeds ~253V. High voltage can damage the inverter and compressor, so the unit shuts down.

Call the utility or an electrician to investigate.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm high-voltage condition with a meter.

fixSteps.title: Contact utility
fixSteps.instruction: If service voltage is high, call utility.

faq.q: Could it be a neutral problem?
faq.a: Yes - a broken service neutral can cause high phase voltage.

title: Outdoor Unit Communication Failure
shortDescription: iComfort/iHarmony bus lost communication with outdoor unit.
fullDescription: E290 means the indoor equipment interface cannot reach the outdoor unit over the RSBus. Typical causes are miswired terminals, missing outdoor power, or a failed outdoor communications chip.

fixSteps.title: Check RSBus wires
fixSteps.instruction: Verify R, i+, i- and C continuity.

faq.a: Lennox uses i+/i-/R/C labeling - match by name, not color.

title: Outdoor Unit Incompatible / Wrong Model
shortDescription: iComfort detected an incompatible outdoor unit.
fullDescription:
E294 means the outdoor unit doesn't match the indoor/equipment profile. This often appears after replacing one component with a non-matching model or after a firmware issue.

Re-run equipment setup and confirm compatibility on Lennox's AHRI matchup.

faq.q: Can I mix older Lennox with iComfort?
faq.a: Only certain generations - consult Lennox matchup tool.

title: Compressor High Pressure
shortDescription: Compressor stopped due to high-pressure switch trip.
fullDescription:
E400 indicates the high-pressure switch has opened. Usually caused by dirty outdoor coil (cooling) or blocked indoor airflow (heating).

After multiple trips the system locks out with E410.

faq.a: No - the switch protects the system.

title: Compressor Low Pressure
fullDescription: E403 indicates the low-pressure switch has tripped, usually from refrigerant loss. After 3 trips in an hour the system locks out with E412.

fixSteps.title: Call for service
fixSteps.instruction: Pro will perform leak search and charge correction.

faq.a: No - EPA license required and leak must be fixed.

title: High Pressure Lockout
shortDescription: Repeated E400 trips - system locked out.
fullDescription:
E410 is a lockout after the high-pressure switch opened three or more times. Manual reset required.

Fix the root cause (airflow or charge) before resetting.

faq.a: Protects compressor from repeated stress.

title: Low Pressure Lockout
shortDescription: Repeated E403 trips - system locked out.
fullDescription: E412 occurs after multiple low-pressure trips. Manual reset required; root cause is almost always refrigerant loss.

faq.q: Will it clear on its own?
faq.a: No, manual reset after repair.

title: Compressor Inverter Fault
fullDescription:
E420 on Lennox variable-capacity heat pumps (like XP25) indicates an inverter drive fault - overcurrent, overtemperature, or drive communication error.

Usually requires drive or compressor diagnostics by a Lennox-trained technician.

faq.a: Not always - often the inverter drive is the failure.

title: Outdoor Thermistor Open/Short
shortDescription: Outdoor air or coil thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E433 means a Lennox outdoor temperature sensor has failed open or shorted. The sensors used are 10k ohm NTC thermistors.

Locate the indicated sensor (ambient or coil) and replace if resistance is out of range.

faq.a: Ambient hangs free near intake; coil is clipped to a return bend.

title: Inverter Communication Loss
shortDescription: Communication lost between control and inverter board.
fullDescription: Error E105 on Lennox iComfort heat pumps means the main control cannot communicate with the inverter compressor drive. The system shuts down to protect the compressor.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect both indoor and outdoor power for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Check RSBus
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect 4-wire communication cable end to end.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat communication plugs at both boards.

fixSteps.title: Call Lennox Tech
fixSteps.instruction: Inverter board diagnostics require Lennox iComfort tools.

whenToCallPro: iComfort inverter systems require Lennox-trained technicians with proper diagnostic tools.

faq.a: Lennox's proprietary communication bus between equipment and thermostat.
Lennox specifies 18-gauge stranded thermostat cable for RSBus.
Inverter boards are $400-$700 plus labor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wires

fixSteps.instruction: Should match Lennox thermistor curve at ambient.

title: Liquid Line Sensor Fault

fixSteps.instruction: Ensure good contact with copper tubing.

fixSteps.instruction: Compare to ambient line temp curve.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault

fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor sits firmly against coil hairpin.

fixSteps.title: Check Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Look for damage or rodent chew.

fixSteps.title: Replace

Only to its OEM location with proper thermal contact.

title: High Pressure Switch Trip

title: Low Line Voltage
fullDescription: The control board has detected that incoming line voltage is below the minimum required for compressor operation.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: E115 shown on display or remote
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

title: E500 — Compressor RPS Sensor Open
shortDescription: Compressor refrigerant pressure sensor reads outside valid range.
fullDescription: Lennox iComfort communicating heat pumps use a 0-680 psi pressure transducer on the suction side. E500 fires when the signal is below 0.4V or above 4.6V — implying open circuit or short.

fixSteps.title: Reseat plug
fixSteps.instruction: Three-wire Molex at compressor — push until clicks.

fixSteps.title: Check 5VDC supply
fixSteps.instruction: Red wire should read 5VDC to common with breaker on.

fixSteps.title: Replace transducer
fixSteps.instruction: Lennox 100269-04; install with EPA refrigerant recovery if Schrader does not seal.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant recovery required for transducer replacement.

faq.a: Yes — runs in single-stage backup until repaired.

title: E600 — Demand-Defrost Algorithm Failure
shortDescription: Defrost cycle initiated but coil did not clear within max time.
fullDescription: E600 occurs when Lennox demand-defrost runs for max time (10 min) and outdoor coil sensor never reached 50F termination temperature. Likely cause: low charge, failed reversing valve, or blocked coil.
symptoms: Outdoor coil remains iced after defrost

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off, let coil thaw 1 hour, restart and observe.

fixSteps.title: Reversing valve test
fixSteps.instruction: Listen for 'whoosh' on defrost initiation — silence = stuck valve.

fixSteps.title: Charge verification
fixSteps.instruction: Tech to weigh charge against nameplate using subcool method.

faq.a: Yes — until repaired, set to EM HEAT to avoid further coil damage.

title: E601 — Reversing Valve Sense Mismatch
shortDescription: Liquid and suction sensor temperatures inconsistent with commanded mode.
fullDescription: E601 means after reversing valve command, the sensor pair did not swap their temperature pattern. Commonly indicates valve slug stuck mid-position or sensors wired to wrong line.

fixSteps.title: Verify wire colors
fixSteps.instruction: Liquid sensor (typically yellow) on liquid line; suction (blue) on suction.

fixSteps.title: Tap valve body
fixSteps.instruction: During call, lightly strike valve with mallet to free slug.

whenToCallPro: Reversing valve replacement requires brazing and refrigerant recovery.

faq.q: How long does the valve last?
faq.a: 15-20 years typical. Failures before that often due to debris in system.

title: E624 — Compressor Hard Lockout
shortDescription: Three identical compressor faults within 1 hour — locked out.
fullDescription: Lennox iComfort locks out the compressor after 3 strikes of the same fault (e.g., low pressure, high pressure) within 60 minutes. Manual reset at thermostat is required.

fixSteps.title: Identify root fault
fixSteps.instruction: Scroll through history on iComfort installer menu.

fixSteps.title: Address root
fixSteps.instruction: Lockout returns until underlying issue fixed.

whenToCallPro: Repeated lockouts in 24h require professional diagnosis.

faq.a: No — repeated resets without diagnosis can damage compressor.

title: E700 — Outdoor Fan ECM Communication Loss
shortDescription: Communicating ECM outdoor fan motor not responding to drive board.
fullDescription: Lennox uses ECM outdoor fans on iComfort heat pumps. E700 fires when the motor controller stops reporting RPM/torque to the main board within 5 seconds of a call.

fixSteps.title: Reseat 5-pin
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect breaker, unplug and reseat motor harness.

fixSteps.title: Spin test
fixSteps.instruction: By hand, motor should spin freely with no grinding.

fixSteps.title: Module replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Lennox motors have replaceable ECM module - P/N varies.

faq.q: Can I use a PSC fan instead?
faq.a: No — communicating system requires ECM with feedback.

title: E705 — Outdoor Fan ECM Overtorque
shortDescription: ECM fan reported torque exceeded limit — likely obstruction.
fullDescription: E705 fires when the ECM outdoor fan reports torque above safe threshold for 30 seconds. Causes: ice on blade, debris (leaves) jammed in fan, or bearing damage.

fixSteps.title: De-energize
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker before any access to fan blade.

fixSteps.title: Inspect bearings
fixSteps.instruction: Spin by hand - should be smooth, no wobble.

whenToCallPro: If bearing wobble felt, motor replacement needed.

faq.a: Repeated overtorque shortens bearing life - clear obstruction quickly.

title: E710 — Compressor Inverter Drive Overcurrent
shortDescription: Inverter compressor drive measured current above limit.
fullDescription: On Lennox SL25XPV variable-capacity heat pumps, E710 is reported by the inverter drive when compressor current exceeds rated max. Causes include locked rotor, low voltage start, or refrigerant flood-back.
symptoms: Compressor will not start or trips quickly

fixSteps.title: Verify crankcase heater
fixSteps.instruction: Should be warm to touch after 24h power-on.

fixSteps.title: Allow heat soak
fixSteps.instruction: Power on with compressor disabled for 8 hours, then attempt restart.

fixSteps.title: Drive replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If trips after heat soak, drive or compressor likely damaged.

whenToCallPro: Inverter drive replacement requires Lennox-trained tech.

faq.a: Warming the compressor crankcase to boil off liquid refrigerant before starting.

safetyWarning: Inverter drives store 600VDC bus voltage for several minutes after power-off.

title: E720 — Outdoor Ambient Sensor Open
fullDescription: E720 means the outdoor ambient sensor (used for balance-point control with auxiliary heat) is open or shorted. The system reverts to a default 35F balance point.
symptoms: Auxiliary heat runs at higher temperatures

fixSteps.title: Locate sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Mounted on outdoor cabinet, shielded from sun.

whenToCallPro: If wiring routed through inaccessible conduit.

faq.a: Yes, but with higher electric resistance heat usage.

title: E801 — iComfort Communication Loss to Outdoor
shortDescription: Indoor thermostat lost RSBus communication with outdoor unit.
fullDescription: E801 fires when the iComfort thermostat cannot reach the outdoor unit on the 4-wire RSBus communicating cable for more than 60 seconds.

causes.cause: Loose connection at iHarmony / outdoor lug
Wire run too long without repeater
Failed RSBus chip on outdoor board

symptoms: Comm icon shows X on iComfort

fixSteps.title: Reseat both ends
fixSteps.instruction: Power off both ends, reseat all 4 wires (R/i+/i-/C) at indoor and outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Verify polarity
fixSteps.instruction: i+ to i+, i- to i- — common installation error.

fixSteps.title: Check 24V at outdoor
fixSteps.instruction: R-C should show 24VAC at outdoor terminal block.

whenToCallPro: Long wire runs may need shielded cable or repeater.

faq.q: Can I use thermostat wire for this?
faq.a: Lennox specifies their RSBus cable; standard 18/4 thermostat works for short runs.

title: E901 — Defrost Sensor Drift
shortDescription: Defrost sensor reads inconsistent values vs. ambient.
fullDescription: E901 is a soft warning: defrost coil sensor reading is suspicious (e.g., reads warmer than ambient when unit is off). Often indicates loose strap on coil or sensor wire damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect strap
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor should be firmly clipped to a clean copper return bend on bottom of coil.

fixSteps.title: Re-strap
fixSteps.instruction: Apply thermal paste, secure with metal clip; tuck wire away from sun.

whenToCallPro: Repeated drift after restrapping suggests sensor failure.

faq.a: Soft warning — system runs, but defrost timing degrades.
